name: South London Gallery
funding: Ongoing support from Arts Council England, Southwark Council, Bukhman Foundation, Bloomberg Philanthropies and Garfield Weston Foundation. Corporate partners include Artsy and Bloomberg; galleries and patrons also give.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies funds it; 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg in May 2026. SLG returned a Sackler gift in 2018.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the current supporters page names funders undated, and the trustees are listed.

name: Studio Voltaire
funding: Arts Council England core funding; Mayor of London; trusts including Wolfson, Garfield Weston, Foyle and Henry Moore Foundation; corporate patrons BakerMcKenzie and Fletcher Gallery Services; a Council of supporters.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies supported its website through the Digital Accelerator Programme. 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg in May 2026.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the supporters and funders page names funders undated, and trustees are listed.

name: Tate Modern
funding: £120M (group). DCMS statutory grant-in-aid, Bank of America, Hyundai Motor, Uniqlo, philanthropic circles.
watch: Ended BP in 2016 after protests; Sackler name removed 2022.
why_flagged: Ended BP in 2016 after protests; Sackler name removed 2022.
records_note: Parent Tate posts accounts from 2010-11 to 2025-26 and annual reports, names supporters in its 2025-26 report, and lists its trustees.

name: Wellcome Collection
watch: Name to know: Wellcome Trust, whose fossil-fuel investments drew a 2015 divestment campaign; it sold BP and Shell shares in 2022.
why_flagged: Name to know: Wellcome Trust, whose fossil-fuel investments drew a 2015 divestment campaign; it sold BP and Shell shares in 2022.
records_note: No records of its own; its parent Wellcome Trust publishes annual reports and accounts 2019 to 2025 and its governors, and names no donors.

name: Whitechapel Gallery
funding: Arts Council England funds it. The 2021-22 report names Bloomberg Philanthropies, Max Mara, Swarovski Foundation and City Bridge Trust as major donors; Bloomberg and Phillips are corporate patrons.
watch: Historic East London public gallery founded in 1901.
why_flagged: Bloomberg Philanthropies is campaigned against elsewhere, not at Whitechapel. A 2006 Bellmer show lost works after self-censorship claims; no later case found.
records_note: No annual reports on its site; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the Thank You page names donors undated, and trustees are listed.

name: Hammer Museum
funding: UCLA operational partnership, free admission endowment, Mellon Foundation, patrons.
watch: Built and endowed by Occidental Petroleum.
why_flagged: Built and endowed by Occidental Petroleum.
records_note: It posts audited financial statements for 2024 and names capital campaign donors for 2016 to 2025 and its board, but no annual reports.

name: Museum of Jurassic Technology
funding: Expenses $0.6M (FY2023); members, founder David Wilson, Getty and Mike Kelley Foundation grants 2024, LA city and county arts funds.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Bloomberg Philanthropies appears only on a donors page dated 1996 to 2001; no current roster published. Bloomberg Philanthropies is on the only published foundation roster, which is undated. That name dates the list after 2006, despite the page's 1996-2001 footer.
records_note: No annual reports found; Form 990s for 2011 to 2023 are on ProPublica, one undated page names foundation funders, and no board is listed.

name: The Broad
watch: Director Bruce Karatz, ex-KB Home chief, settled SEC option-backdating charges in 2008 and received probation in 2010.
why_flagged: Director Bruce Karatz, ex-KB Home chief, settled SEC option-backdating charges in 2008 and received probation in 2010.
records_note: No annual reports, donor list or board on its site; Form 990-PF filings for 2010 to 2023 are public on ProPublica.

name: Bonnefanten
funding: Province of Limburg, the culture ministry and VriendenLoterij give structural support. Mondriaan Fund, Ammodo and others add project money. Over 150,000 visitors a year.
watch: Provincial public art museum governed under Dutch cultural sector transparency regulations.
records_note: Bonnefanten's ANBI page posts annual reports with accounts for 2017 to 2025 and names its supervisory board; the 2025 report names its funders.

name: Museo del Prado
funding: 3.5M visitors (2025). Benefactors Fundación BBVA (2025) and Fundación AXA (2024); Fundación Iberdrola España funds fellowships to 2027; Fundación Endesa, Rassini and la Caixa (to 2025) fund projects.
watch: Utilities Iberdrola (66% renewable capacity) and Endesa fund programmes; both sell gas. la Caixa's holding Criteria owns 28.5% of gas utility Naturgy.
records_note: Its site answers every request with a Cloudflare check, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be read; only BOE funder agreements were opened.

name: Museo Reina Sofía
funding: State museum. Corporate patrons: Inditex, Fundación la Caixa, Fundación Mapfre, Fundación Mutua Madrileña. Partners include Estrella Damm, HP, Iberia, Madrid city and region.
watch: National museum of modern art in Madrid.
why_flagged: la Caixa's holding Criteria is the largest shareholder of gas utility Naturgy, 23% of its 2025 dividends. No Repsol, Endesa or Iberdrola listed.
records_note: It posts annual activity reports 2002 to 2025, yearly accounts, a named sponsors page and the Real Patronato members.

name: The Whitworth
funding: University of Manchester gallery. Funders include Arts Council England, Research England, National Lottery Heritage Fund and Friends of the Whitworth; corporate: Hyundai Motor Company, Little Greene, Frieze x Deutsche Bank.
watch: In 2021 university management removed Forensic Architecture's Palestine statement and the show closed three days. In 2022, 23 artists withdrew from British Art Show 9.
records_note: Names sponsors and funders with no date; posts no annual report, accounts or board of its own, as the University of Manchester runs it.
